resources.string: Stop Facebook photos from flooding Google Photos

Facebook saves photos and videos into your phone\'s camera roll folder (DCIM/Facebook on most phones). Google Photos treats that folder as part of your camera roll and backs everything up — often within seconds.
This app watches that folder in real time and moves each new file into a separate Facebook_Saved folder within milliseconds of it being written, deleting the original from DCIM/Facebook before Google Photos gets a chance to sync it. A small persistent notification keeps this watcher alive; a 15-minute backup check also runs in case the watcher ever gets restarted by the system.
To do this it needs \"All files access\" — without it, Android blocks apps from deleting files they didn\'t create themselves, which is the \"permission denied\" error you may have hit before.
✅ All files access granted. Real-time watcher is active, plus a 15-minute backup sweep.
⚠️ All files access not granted yet. Nothing can be moved or deleted without it.
